Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: BR Analytics — onboarding model plan & token scan

Hi team,

Looping you all in for the implementation handoff for Blue Ridge Analytics (BR). They want to ship two features in phase 1: a short-form summary API for ingestion (batch enrichment) and a chat-assist endpoint for analyst workflows. High level:

- Primary constraints: PII retention policy (30 days), must support EU data region later, and SLA target is 99.9% for the analyst chat during business hours.
- Expected traffic (from BR product): see attached sample logs -> br-analytics-token-scan.csv. Key takeaways from their ops: ~300 batch jobs/day (avg 2k tokens input + 800 tokens output), and chat usage expected to ramp to ~500 active analysts with peak concurrency ~40 sessions, average 1.2k input + 600 tokens generated per session.

Requesting a recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs quality), suggested context window for each feature, rough token-volume cost estimate (monthly), and an initial capacity recommendation (GPU types / instance counts) so we can propose the mutual action plan. Please cc the BR contacts.

Target: get a brief we can share with the customer by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Re: BR Analytics — onboarding model plan & token scan

On Mon, 12 Mar 2028 at 09:02 AM Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Looping you all in for the implementation handoff for Blue Ridge Analytics (BR)...
> Requesting a recommended model shortlist ...

Thanks Hannah — reviewed the sample token traces and put together an initial recommendation below. High-level approach: two model profiles (batch enrichment and interactive chat). For each profile I provide: recommended models, context length, perf/quality expectation, monthly token estimate, and conservative capacity starting point.

Batch enrichment (offline jobs)
- Primary need: high throughput, predictable unit cost, tolerate slightly higher latency (secs).
- Candidates: 
  1) Mistral-12B-instruct (quantized to 4-bit) — best mix of instruction quality and price; good for longer single-doc summarization.
  2) Llama-2-13B-chat (8-bit q) — higher quality on nuanced prompts, small latency hit.
- Recommended context: 8k (covers typical documents from traces).
- Token profile (monthly - conservative): 300 jobs/day * (2k in + 800 out) * 30 = ~25.2M tokens/month.
- Capacity suggestion: 2 x 80GB GPUs (DGX-style) or 3 x 48GB with multi-worker batching; enable continuous batching and prefix caching for repeated doc headers.

Interactive analyst chat (low-latency)
- Primary need: low tail latency (<350ms 95th), high coherence for multi-turn; active context reuse (KV cache) helpful.
- Candidates: 
  1) Redwood-7B-CHAT-16k (4-bit) — strong latency/cost; use for baseline.
  2) Llama-2-70B-chat (quantized 8-bit/sparsely offloaded) — for premium quality mode (fallback when available).
- Recommended context: start with 16k for first pass; plan to expand to 32k in phase 2 if they require large session history for regulatory artifacting.
- Token profile (monthly - conservative): 500 active analysts, average 3 sessions/day, avg 1.8k tokens roundtrip per session => 500*3*1.8k*30 = ~81M tokens/month.
- Capacity suggestion: target 6-8 x 80GB GPU-equivalents behind an autoscaling pool with burst capacity; use quantized runtime, stream small responses, and set per-route concurrency limits.

Cost/latency notes
- Batch jobs can be queued and batched aggressively, so unit cost can be reduced ~2-3x vs chat.
- Chat SLO will drive the biggest infra cost; recommend enabling a small premium tier for analysts with fallback to smaller model variant.

Operational items
- Data residency: customer will want EU region in Q2; plan for model buckets in eu-west-1.
- PII retention: set request/response logs TTL to 30 days; redact sensitive fields pre-ingest (we should provide a small webhook filter template).

Attachments: br-model-shortlist-ops-notes.md (notes on kernel choices, batching knobs), br-analytics-token-scan.csv (reference).

Next steps: Hannah / Monica to confirm which model pair (cost-first or quality-first) BR prefers and whether phase 1 includes the premium quality fallback. I can sketch a cost projection table once they confirm.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BR Analytics — onboarding model plan & token scan

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Context: for analyst sessions we plan to keep the last 10–15 documents (~5–10k tokens) in session history; we will prefer a larger context if it doesn't double cost.
2) Peak concurrency: earlier internal estimate was 40 concurrent sessions during EOD reporting windows — we can pilot with 25 concurrently.
3) For the batch enrichment, some jobs include multiple short docs in a single job (up to ~6k input tokens); please call that out in sizing.

Can we schedule a 30-min technical sizing call Thurs at 10am PT? Also please include a short mutual action plan with milestones, we need that for procurement approval.

- Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Product — Blue Ridge Analytics
emily@br-analytics.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@br-analytics.com>, Raj Kapur <raj.kapur@br-analytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BR Analytics — onboarding model plan & token scan

Emily — thanks, confirmed for Thurs 10am PT. I've attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for procurement, SOC-2 evidence handoff, and phase 1 go-live gating items. Highlights / decisions to be made on the call:

- Phase 1 model decision: cost-first (Redwood-7B-CHAT + Mistral-12B quant) vs quality-first (Llama-2-70B fallback).
- Pilot concurrency: start with 25 concurrent chat sessions; we will scale to 40 during EOD windows by week 3 of the pilot.
- Batch job handling: support up to 6k input per job; will route to the batch pool with 8k context and fall back to sharded processing if >8k.
- Data residency & retention: initial deployment in us-west-2; EU region planned Q2. Logs TTL set to 30 days; we will provide webhook redaction template during onboarding.

Action items ahead of Thurs call:
- Dylan: prepare a short cost-per-token table for the two model pairs and a rough GPU count for pilot.
- Ben: prepare the provisioning template and estimated lead time for dedicated capacity (if they prefer reserved nodes).
- Monica: include the SOC-2 evidence checklist and the sample MSA/term highlights for procurement.
- Emily/Raj: confirm procurement attendee and any procurement deadlines.

Attached: mutual-action-plan.docx. HubSpot link to deal above.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
Hannah
